summary: 昭宗第九子；天祐元年昭宗被弑，朱全忠立之，年十三；天祐二年白马驿之祸，全忠杀朝士三十余人投河；天祐四年禅位于朱全忠，唐亡，梁建；降封后遇害。
summary_en: Ninth son of Zhaozong; after Zhaozong's slaying in the 1st year of Tianyou, Zhu Quanzhong set him up at thirteen; in the 2nd year came the Baimayi disaster, Quanzhong drowning over thirty courtiers in the river; in the 4th year he abdicated to Quanzhong — Tang perished and Liang arose — and, reduced in rank, was done to death.

bio_md:
# 唐哀帝 · 主要事迹

李柷（初名祚），昭宗第九子。天祐元年，朱全忠弑昭宗，立柷，年十三。哀帝在位三年，实为朱全忠掌中之物：天祐二年，全忠杀朝士裴枢、独孤损等三十余人，投尸于白马驿黄河——「白马驿之祸」，清流之祸，唐室士大夫精英尽丧。

天祐四年，朱全忠逼哀帝禅位，唐亡，后梁建立——唐自高祖武德元年开国，历二十一帝二百九十年而终。哀帝降封济阴王，次年（开平二年）为朱全忠所害，年十七。

史评哀帝：「幼冲亡国，唐三百年终。」唐之亡，不亡于哀帝之世，而亡于安史之乱后藩镇、宦官、党争之积弊：僖宗之播迁、昭宗之被弑、白马驿之祸，皆其亡之序曲。哀帝不过承其祸而已。「唐亡」之日，中国历史进入五代十国之局。

> 参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷020下《哀帝纪》、新五代史卷001《梁本纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Zhu, first named Zuo, was the ninth son of Zhaozong. In the 1st year of Tianyou, Zhu Quanzhong slew Zhaozong and set up Zhu, aged thirteen. Three years he reigned, a thing of Quanzhong's: in the 2nd year of Tianyou Quanzhong slew the courtiers Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, and over thirty others, throwing their bodies into the Yellow River at the Baima relay — the Baimayi disaster, the "slaughter of the clear stream," the elite of the Tang court lost at a stroke.

In the 4th year of Tianyou Quanzhong forced the abdication: Tang fell, and the Later Liang arose — from Gaozu's founding in the 1st year of Wude, twenty-one emperors and two hundred and ninety years of Tang were at an end. Ai, reduced to Prince of Jiyin, was done to death by Quanzhong the next year (the 2nd of Kaiping), aged seventeen.

The histories say: "a child at the fall of the realm — the three hundred years of Tang were at an end." Tang did not fall in Ai's reign but to the long disease of feudatories, eunuchs, and factionalism since the An–Shi rebellion: Xizong's flight, Zhaozong's slaying, the Baimayi disaster were its funeral march. Ai only inherited the catastrophe. With "the fall of Tang," Chinese history entered the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 20b ("Benji of Emperor Ai"), and the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 1 ("Annals of Liang").
